Alex.note: I'm Meowfia, and Casey is the likely Meowfia liar. Throwing at Casey could eggsecute a partner, so I'll throw one low card at Blair, a Farm-looking player, to stay out of the Casey vote.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Hawk claims in round 3 conflicted over Finley's visitors, and the nest changes never settled it. Nothing else was unclear.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: my Falcon read exposed Drew's false Blair claim, and the table voted Drew out.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports show who visited you, so visit claims could be checked instead of argued.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I threw at Finley, who was Meowfia, but Finley's votes tied me into elimination; I should have kept more cards to throw at Ellis instead.

Blair.confusing: The Floofer's hug was the hidden piece: a hugged visitor's Hawk gains nothing and the Eagle reads zero. That made Casey's true visit look false, and I couldn't tell it apart from a lie.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Alex and Finley threw at each other and the votes tied, flipping the eggsecution to Farm. The table's cross-checking of nest counts was sharp.
Blair.change: Make the dawn report say when a visitor was hugged or blocked, so Eagle and Hawk claims can be checked against it.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Casey, who was actually Farm, and lost them. I should have thrown one low card, since Finley's Floofer hug explained the zero and I had no proof against Casey.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle and Falcon reports conflicted with real visits, and I couldn't tell whether the nests or the claims were wrong. Nest changes only show visitors to the target, which made it hard to verify who visited whom.
Casey.fun: Round 1 was the most fun: Finley, Blair, and I cross-checked egg sources and the table turned on Drew's visit claim. Watching the Turkey and Hawk claims collide was a good puzzle.
Casey.change: I would make the dawn reports show who visited the player, not only the egg count, so visit claims could be checked directly. That would cut down on the guessing about who is lying.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw my Wild at Drew based on a nest-count dispute and ended up eggsecuted. I would have held my cards and asked Blair and Ellis to explain why their claims lined up against me before throwing anything.

Drew.confusing: Which nest changes came from which visits, since Eagle and Hawk gains depended on whose nest was counted, and the table argued about it for several turns.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when I was the Sphinx: Alex and Blair spent the day arguing over who visited whom while the nest counts kept testing their claims.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports more explicit about which visits changed which nests, so players spend less time untangling who gained from whom.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw two cards at Alex, a Farm player, when Finley was the Meowfia Sphinx; I should have thrown at Finley.

Ellis.confusing: The visit counts were hard to trust: an Eagle gains from its target's visitors, not its own, and several players misread that, which made the nest-count checks unreliable.
Ellis.fun: Round 3's back-and-forth over whether Casey's Hawk visit showed up in Drew's Eagle nest was a tense standoff, and watching the table split on it was enjoyable.
Ellis.change: Include the visitor names in each dawn report for visit-based roles, so players can check claims without relying on nest-size arithmetic.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey on the strength of Drew's unverified zero-visitor claim, and Casey was Farm. I should have held my cards or thrown at Drew, since I had no evidence against Casey beyond a single conflicting report.

Finley.confusing: The Sphinx role was hard to use: I learned farm roles but had no clear way to tell which farm player held a role without visiting. Round-to-round role changes also made claims hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 1's egg-count debate was the best moment: Blair and Drew contradicted each other, and the nest numbers exposed who was lying.
Finley.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited you, so visit claims can be checked without guesswork.
Finley.regret: As Sphinx in round 2 I kept my target private and let Alex and Ellis take the blame, when I could have steered the vote toward the Farm players claiming false visits.

review.title: The Silent Hug
review.headline: Hugs blanked the Farm's evidence twice, and Meowfia walked off with the last two rounds.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win. Blair's Turkey nest check showed Drew never visited him, and Drew was eggsecuted. In rounds 2 and 3 two Meowfia teams each got a Farm player eggsecuted. Round 2 was a 3-3 tie that the tie rule gave to Meowfia. In round 3 the Floofer's hugs silently blanked the Eagle and Hawk, and the table convicted an honest Hawk. Alex, a Meowfia who threw only one card, won with 13.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) and Drew (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Alex's Falcon report said Drew visited Ellis, and Drew's story (he visited Blair) failed against Blair's Turkey, since Drew's nest was +0. Four players threw at Drew. Casey threw at her own teammate without knowing it. Farm won.

Blair (Floofer) and Finley (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Blair hugged his own partner, which blanked Finley's Sphinx. Blair claimed Pigeon and Finley backed him, though Finley's single egg really came from Ellis's Turkey. Votes ended 3-3 between Alex (Farm) and Finley (Meowfia), and the tie rule eggsecuted Alex. Drew's two-card throw made the tie. Both winners threw Wilds and scored 0.

Alex (Mouser) and Finley (Floofer) were Meowfia. Finley's hug, plus the hugs given to visitors, blanked Casey's Hawk and Drew's Eagle. Drew's honest +0 then clashed with Casey's honest Hawk claim. Everyone piled on Casey, and Alex fed the fire. Casey was Farm, so Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Blair's Turkey logic traps Drew: a visitor would have gained an egg, Drew's nest is +0, so his claimed visit is a lie.
Casey, a Meowfia who doesn't know her partner, throws a Wild at Drew and helps eggsecute her own teammate.
The vote ties 3-3 and the tie rule eggsecutes Farm Alex. Drew's two-card throw is what made the tie.
The hugs make two honest players look like liars. Casey and Drew each tell the truth and each accuses the other, and Casey is eggsecuted.

confusions.what: Said nobody visited him, forgetting that a Turkey's visitors are exactly why other players gained eggs. He retracted it.
Argued that his Hawk egg proved Blair was Meowfia. He forgot the Turkey also pays visitors, then conceded.
Thought a Sphinx visits a chosen player (Blair). He also read Ellis's +0 as 'no visitors to Ellis', but the Eagle's eggs count visitors to its target.
Threw at Blair because Blair's nest was +0 despite two visitors. A Turkey's own nest doesn't change.
Concluded Blair had no visitors from her +0 as Eagle. Casey herself had visited Blair, and her Eagle was hugged.
Asked Casey whether Tit or Eagle was true, forgetting roles are re-dealt each round. He also said 'nobody visited me' as Turkey, which he cannot know.
Treated Alex's round 1 Falcon claim as a contradiction with his own Falcon role. Roles are re-dealt.
Accepted that Blair's Pigeon explained Finley's egg. Ellis's Turkey could equally have paid Finley, and nobody noticed the single egg couldn't cover both.
Said the Eagle gains from visitors to itself, not to its target. He corrected himself later.
Took her +0 Hawk result to mean Finley was Farm. Her Hawk was hugged, so the result meant nothing.
Took his +0 Eagle result to mean Finley had no visitors. His Eagle was hugged.

worked: Turkey: a visitor gets paid and the Turkey's own nest stays flat. That made Blair's round 1 check on Drew simple and fair, and it produced the best deduction in the game.
Meowfia not knowing each other: Casey throwing at her teammate in round 1, and Finley's round 3 worry about hitting a partner, were real tense moments.
Throw counts being public: Drew's two-card throw decided round 2, and Blair and Drew's two-card throws in round 3 clearly signalled the pile-on.
Consolation return of the highest card: Alex, Casey and Ellis kept value by throwing at the right team, which rewards guessing even in a loss.
problems: Hugged: the dawn report doesn't tell you that you were hugged. A hugged Hawk or Eagle sees a plain +0, which looks like real evidence. In round 3 one Floofer blanked three players and got an honest Farm Hawk eggsecuted. Fix: tell hugged players they were hugged, or at least that their result may be unreliable.
Tie rule: ties go against a tied Farm player. In round 2 a 3-3 tie decided the round for Meowfia. Consider a fixed tie-break, or make the rule less lopsided.

Scoring: winning with Wilds and 1-point cards pays about nothing. In round 2 both winners scored 0, and Alex won the game by throwing one low card a round. Hoarding beats risk, so winning a round feels hollow. Fix: raise the pay for a win or set a minimum throw value.

The Mouser's Wink was never used (Casey in round 1, Alex in round 3), so it did nothing. Winks are rare and the Mouser's info is weak. Fix: give Meowfia a stronger reason to use it, or let the Mouser learn something more useful.

Day talk is repetitive and rules-confused. Players kept asking about roles from earlier rounds and mixing up Eagle and Turkey eggs. The same accusation was repeated until 'nothing to add' ended the talk. Fix: put a one-line reminder in the round header that roles are re-dealt, and add a quick Eagle and Turkey cheat sheet.
